Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support roughly a quarter of all marine species. They form when tiny animals called polyps build hard calcium carbonate skeletons that accumulate over centuries. Rising sea temperatures cause corals to expel the algae that feed them, a process known as bleaching. Pollution, overfishing and ocean acidification add further stress, and scientists warn that many reefs could be lost within decades without sharp cuts to carbon emissions.
